name: South Mumbai Heritage Walk by MDT
description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The Hanging Garden is one of the most beautiful and well-maintained green spaces in Mumbai. The garden is quite large and spacious, offering plenty of room for visitors to relax, walk, and enjoy nature.

One of its biggest attractions is the excellent children’s play area, which has ample space for kids to run around and enjoy themselves. The dedicated walking paths make it a great spot for morning and evening walks, fitness activities, or simply spending quality time outdoors.

The garden is filled with lush greenery, beautiful landscaping, and a wide variety of trees that provide shade and a refreshing atmosphere. The peaceful environment makes it a perfect escape from the busy city life.

Whether you’re visiting with family, children, or friends, Hanging Garden offers something for everyone. The clean surroundings, open spaces, and abundance of greenery make it an ideal destination for relaxation and recreation. Highly recommended for nature lovers and families looking for a pleasant outing.

featured_reviews.name: Unscripted India
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hanging Gardens is one of those places in Mumbai that every tourist should visit at least once. Located on Malabar Hill, this garden offers a perfect mix of nature, fresh air, and stunning city views. As soon as you enter, you feel a sense of calm away from the busy streets and traffic of Mumbai.
The garden is beautifully maintained with lush green lawns, colorful flowers, and creatively shaped hedges, including animal figures that are great for photos. Walking through the garden pathways is a pleasant experience, especially with the cool breeze that flows throughout the day. The highlight for most visitors is the breathtaking view of South Mumbai and Marine Drive from the top. During sunset, the sky changes colors and the city lights slowly come alive, making it a truly memorable sight.
Hanging Gardens is a great place for tourists traveling with family, couples, or even solo visitors who want to relax and enjoy scenic views. There are plenty of seating areas to sit, relax, and soak in the surroundings. The place is clean, well organized, and safe.
It can get crowded during weekends and holidays, so visiting early in the morning or on a weekday is recommended. Overall, Hanging Gardens is a peaceful, scenic, and refreshing tourist attraction that beautifully showcases Mumbai from a different perspective.

Hanging Garden is a place I’ve been hearing about since my childhood. It was always on my list, because no one had ever taken me there before. Visiting it now felt really nice.

We usually think of South Bombay as a place where rich people live, but I feel that richness comes from places like this. The garden is so neat and clean, beautifully maintained, with red soil all around. You can actually see people constantly taking care of it so that everyone can use and enjoy the space properly.

There aren’t any fancy exercise machines there—just simple walking, jogging, and running. But walking on red soil in the early morning feels different, it feels better somehow. The garden is huge, with many benches where people sit and relax after their walk.

I saw many senior citizens there for their morning walks, and even handicapped people being brought in by their caretakers. Watching all of this felt really heartwarming. The place is very peaceful—no chaos, no disturbance. At least in the early morning, it felt calm and soothing. I don’t know how it is later in the day, but for me, that morning experience was truly peaceful.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Review of Malabar Hill and Girgaon Beach

Our recent visit to Malabar Hill was inspired by a social media reel by a travel blogger showcasing the new bridge. Unfortunately, the information was inaccurate as the bridge was not open for visitors yet. It seems like the bridge has been overhyped, which was disappointing. So, don’t fall for the hype and waste your time if you’re only visiting for this.

That said, Malabar Hill itself never fails to charm with its timeless appeal. The vintage architecture, well-maintained roads, and excellent traffic management by the Mumbai Police make it a pleasant experience to explore the area.

While at Malabar Hill, we made a stop at Girgaon Beach, which turned out to be the highlight of the trip. If you’re visiting, don’t miss the stunning sunset views—especially in the evening when the beach comes alive with a serene and picturesque atmosphere. It’s truly worth a visit and a great way to end the day.

In summary, while the bridge was a letdown, Malabar Hill and Girgaon Beach still offer plenty of reasons to visit. Go for the classic charm, not the hype!

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Dhobi Ghat for a college street photography project, and honestly, it turned out to be one of the most visually fascinating places I’ve explored in Mumbai. The scale of it all instantly catches your attention — endless rows of clothes, synchronized movement, narrow lanes, textures, colours, and stories unfolding in every corner.

For photography, the place is a goldmine. Every frame feels layered with life, hard work, and rhythm. There’s chaos, but there’s also incredible structure hidden within it. “Beauty lies in the ordinary,” and Dhobi Ghat reflects exactly that through its everyday reality.

What I appreciated most was how authentic and unfiltered the entire place felt. Raw Mumbai in its truest form.

featured_reviews.name: Donggeon Kang
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dhobighat has been operating since 1890 during British colonial rule. From early dawn well past sunset the Dhobi Wallahs work tirelessly washing laundry collected from all across Mumbai. Learning that these workers are considered untouchables  people who fall outside even the caste system. left me standing on that bridge in silence feeling a weight I couldn’t quite shake.

Thousands of years of caste hierarchy pressed into every concrete washing pen. That image stayed with me long after I left.

What struck me most was the view from above. Gleaming luxury high rises tower directly behind this open air laundry where people labor by hand all day for almost nothing. That contrast is not just striking, It is Mumbai in one frame. It is India in one frame.

Come here not just to see it but to feel what it means.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Highly recommend this eye-opening and respectful experience!
